cards.title: Introduction to ASP.NET Core Deployment
cards.content: Deploying an ASP.NET Core application involves publishing the app, packaging its dependencies, and hosting it on a web server or cloud platform like IIS, Kestrel with a reverse proxy (Nginx/Apache), or Azure App Service.

cards.title: Hosting Models
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core supports two primary hosting models:

  • In-process hosting: Runs the app in the same process as the IIS worker process for better performance.
  • Out-of-process hosting: Relies on Kestrel as a web server, typically behind a reverse proxy like IIS, Nginx, or Apache.

cards.title: Containerizing with Docker
cards.content:
Docker allows you to package your ASP.NET Core application with all its dependencies into a container image. This ensures consistent behavior across development, testing, and production environments.

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app

cards.title: Deployment Summary
cards.content: Choosing the right deployment strategy depends on your infrastructure. Whether using IIS on Windows, Nginx with Kestrel on Linux, or Docker containers in Kubernetes, understanding the publish and hosting mechanisms is vital for robust ASP.NET Core applications.
